thread.title: Why this market isn't being driven by just a handful of stocks

author: morningstar.com
title: Why this market isn't being driven by just a handful of stocks
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
It's Friday the 13th, but the bulls should be feeling a bit lucky, given the S&P 500 stands at a five-month high.
Sure, today's earnings from big banks could cast a hex on this market. Plus, we've got that U.S.-U.K. "special relationship" turning extra special.
But our call of the day may embolden the bulls. It tackles a hot topic -- this FAANG-tastic stock market's top heaviness -- and it comes from A Wealth of Common Sense's Ben Carlson, who also throws a bone to the bears.
"The stock market is not currently being driven by just a handful of stocks," writes Carlson, Ritholtz Wealth Management's director of institutional asset management.
One "tell-tale sign that this isn't the case" comes from the fact that small-cap stocks are outperforming this year, he says. The small-fry Russell 2000 is up 10% in 2018, besting the S&P's gain of 4.7%.
Carlson also points to a key indicator for market breadth -- the NYSE Advance-Decline Line. He offers the chart below that plots that gauge's moves alongside the S&P's action.
"If there were only a few stocks rising, you would see a large divergence between these lines," he writes. "Instead, we see the advance-decline fairly in line with the stock market. This tells us that there are far more stocks rising than just a few of the biggest names."
The Michigan-based portfolio manager gives a few caveats as well, including:
-- "We certainly could see what many would call an overdue correction in tech stocks that brings down the rest of the market."
-- "If you're invested solely in a total market or S&P 500 index fund, then yes, your returns will likely be driven by a handful of stocks. This is simply the way market-cap weighting works."
Go here (http://awealthofcommonsense.com/2018/07/concentration-in-the-stock-market/) to read his full post. (H/t Abnormal Returns (https://abnormalreturns.com/2018/07/12/thursday-links-remaining-relevant/))

And see:The tech sector delivered all of the stock market's gains so far in 2018 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-sector-contributed-all-of-the-stock-market-gains-so-far-in-2018-2018-07-02)
Key market gauges
Futures for the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 are little changed, after the Dow , S&P and Nasdaq Composite closed with gains yesterday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-set-for-rebound-ahead-of-inflation-data-2018-07-12), with the tech-laden Naz scoring an all-time high. The three gauges are on track for weekly rises of more than 1%, as of Thursday's close.
European stocks are trading mostly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-hold-to-small-gain-as-techs-rise-with-eye-on-us-bank-earnings-2018-07-13), after Asia largely finished with gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-continue-end-of-the-week-rally-2018-07-12). Oil and gold are dropping, as the dollar index climbs. Bitcoin is changing hands around $6,200.
See the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-poised-for-upbeat-session-as-bank-earnings-steal-center-stage-2018-07-13) for the latest action.
The chart
"The S&P 500 is knocking on the 2,800 door again, and I think we have a much better chance of breaking through this time," technical analyst Mark Arbeter (https://twitter.com/MarkArbeter/status/1017590353552183296) says in a note to clients, as the index sits at its highest closing level since Feb. 1.
The Arbeter Investments president is encouraged in part by that NYSE Advance-Decline Line mentioned earlier. Meanwhile, Elliott Waver Ari Gilburt has been predicting a rally toward 2,800, but then an August pullback (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/technical-charts-point-to-sp-2800-and-then-a-pullback-2018-07-09).
Read more:The stock market's next step could tip the balance toward bears -- or bulls (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-stock-markets-next-step-could-be-its-most-pivotal-2018-07-12)
The Quote:
"If they do a deal like that, we would be dealing with the European Union instead of dealing with the U.K., so it will probably kill the deal." -- President Donald Trump has teed off (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-rips-theresa-may-says-soft-brexit-would-kill-any-future-us-uk-trade-deal-2018-07-12) on British Prime Minister Theresa May's so-called soft Brexit plan.
He is saying that approach would wreck any potential trade pact between the U.S. and the U.K.
His comments appeared late Thursday in the U.K.'s Sun newspaper (https://www.thesun.co.uk/news/6766531/trump-may-brexit-us-deal-off/), which said it had interviewed the president just before he arrived in the land of warm beer. The pound is slumping (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-rises-for-5th-day-as-sterling-slumps-on-trumps-brexit-threat-2018-07-13) following the comments, even as Trump today is sounding friendlier and saying the countries' relationship is "very, very strong." (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-britain-usa-relations/u-s-president-trump-says-relationship-with-uk-is-very-very-strong-idUSKBN1K31CH)
The buzz
J.P. Morgan Chase (JPM)just posted an earnings beat (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jpmorgan-profit-up-18-to-top-estimates-2018-07-13), and Wells Fargo (WFC)and Citigroup (C)are also on tap before the opening bell.
Read more:Banks' earnings are expected to shine, but their stocks may not (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-earnings-are-expected-to-shine-but-their-stocks-may-not-2018-07-10)
Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross has agreed to sell all of his stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wilbur-ross-says-hell-sell-equity-investments-after-inadvertent-errors-2018-07-12) after acknowledging that he failed to sell some holdings as required by ethics agreements.
A jury in St. Louis (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/johnson-johnson-ordered-to-pay-469-billion-in-suit-linking-baby-powder-to-cancer-2018-07-12) found Johnson & Johnson (JNJ)should pay $4.7 billion in damages to 22 women and their families who blamed ovarian-cancer cases on asbestos in the company's iconic baby powder.
There is still buzz around yesterday's extremely contentious hearing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/peter-strzok-says-he-didnt-leak-information-about-trump-russia-probe-before-election-2018-07-12) on Capitol Hill featuring the FBI's Peter Strzok. He testified that he didn't leak damaging information about Trump before the election.
China's trade surplus widened sharply in June (https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/chinas-trade-surplus-widens-in-june-as-imports-drop), as tensions with the U.S. ramped up. Meanwhile, a Shenzhen hotel is denying a report that it was charging Americans an extra 25% (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-china-hotel/chinese-hotel-denies-raising-rates-for-americans-amid-trade-war-idUSKBN1K30RY).
The Justice Department has appealed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/att-stock-dips-after-feds-appeal-time-warner-antitrust-ruling-2018-07-12) a key antitrust ruling that had given a green light to AT&T (T)buyout of Time Warner.
On the U.S. data front, a report on import and export prices is due before the open, and a reading on consumer sentiment is slated to hit once trading gets underway.
The Federal Reserve has a couple of things for us: a monetary policy report, plus the Atlanta Fed's Raphael Bostic doing a Q&A with CPAs. Did he lose a bet or something?
